name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VII
h1: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution VII (CT9A): specs, 4G63T engine and what owners say

us.x: Never sold new in the US; the US got its first Evo, the Evo VIII, in 2003. Cars become legal to import under the 25-year rule once 25 years old by build month, so the first Evo VIIs (on sale in Japan from February 2001) qualify from early 2026.

films.x: Brian O'Conner's lime-green Evo VII, which US Customs gives him for the undercover job; both Mitsubishis turn out to be GPS-tagged. The Evo was not yet sold in the US, so Mitsubishi supplied four cars to the production.

related.t: Lancer Evolution VIII to X, sold in the US

gens.tag: Japan only. 280 PS (276 hp) 4G63T turbo, all-wheel drive with a new active center differential.

variants.name: Lancer Evolution VII GSR

hp.note: 280 PS (206 kW) at 6,500 rpm, JDM; Japan's gentlemen's agreement figure

variants.what: Active Yaw Control, Brembo brakes and a Momo wheel on top of the new active center differential.

variants.name: Lancer Evolution VII RS
variants.what: Stripped rally base car: steel wheels, 15-inch tires, 80 kg lighter than the GSR. AYC was optional.

variants.name: Lancer Evolution VII GT-A
variants.what: Automatic grand tourer version, slightly detuned.

4G63T.name: Mitsubishi 4G63T
facts: 280 PS (276 hp) at 6,500 rpm, 383 Nm (282 lb-ft) at 3,500 rpm

issues.x: RAC's used Evo VII guide says to look for aftermarket fuel cuts or cable ties around the turbo hoses, signs the boost has been raised. It calls the engine itself untemperamental.
Most Evo VIIs have Active Yaw Control, and RAC says servicing it needs Mitsubishi's MUT-II diagnostic tool, so a specialist is the safer bet.

RAC says Japanese-market cars need the 112 mph speed limiter removed, an mph speedometer and odometer, a rear fog light and proper underseal. It also says any trim can be dressed up as another, so check RS and GSR identity.
